title: Scott-continuous model with exactly λβ equational theory
formal: Does there exist a pointed directed-complete partial order D and Scott-continuous maps F:D→[D→D] and L:[D→D]→D with F∘L=id such that, for every pair of finite untyped lambda terms M,N, equality of their interpretations for every environment in D holds if and only if M and N are beta-convertible?
context: This short research proposal states the target identified in the September 2026 fundamental-problem search. The references give the source models and related results. The statement has now received a wording review; a comprehensive review of later results and current open status remains outstanding.

definitions: Terms are generated by variables from a countably infinite set, application MN and abstraction λx.M, modulo renaming bound variables. Beta-convertibility is the least equivalence relation closed under application and abstraction containing (λx.M)N=M[N/x], with capture-avoiding substitution. A directed set is nonempty and every two of its elements have an upper bound in the set. D is a set with a partial order, a least element, and a supremum for every directed subset. Scott-continuous means monotone and preserving directed suprema. [D→D] consists of all Scott-continuous functions, ordered pointwise. An environment ρ assigns an element of D to each variable. Interpret x as ρ(x), MN as F(⟦M⟧ρ)(⟦N⟧ρ), and λx.M as L(d↦⟦M⟧(ρ[x:=d])). The desired condition is ∀M,N: (∀ρ, ⟦M⟧ρ=⟦N⟧ρ) ⇔ M=βN. Models need not be countable, algebraic, effectively presented or extensional; in particular L∘F=id is not required. These are set-based directed-complete orders and all their continuous maps, without a restriction to graph models.
answer_criterion: Prove the proposition in the problem statement or prove its logical negation, using exactly the definitions, hypotheses and quantifier order stated here. The proof must cover the complete target.

sentences: Scott's continuous semantics interprets untyped lambda terms using mathematical domains and continuous functions.
The project asks whether some model identifies exactly the pairs of terms related by beta-conversion.
Beta-conversion expresses equality generated by applying functions to arguments and substituting those arguments into their bodies.
Many semantic constructions validate additional equations, so soundness for beta-reduction alone does not answer the question.
An exact model would show whether this influential notion of continuous meaning can distinguish every pair of terms that the basic operational equations keep separate.
